rationale:
Evidence: iteration 2 is the best raced design (score 41.4; kp 3.0, kd 0.5, ki 0, base 1.4, sensors at x within ±0.04, y 0.04, size 0.012). Every trial in every design so far ended off track, with max_error near 0.06 m, which is the off-track limit. rms_error is steady at about 0.03 m. The s-bend and slalom fail at about 4% progress with almost no seed spread, so the failure is an early, systematic excursion rather than slow drift. Iterations 4 and 5 lowered speed and kp, and oval progress fell from 0.215 to 0.115, so slower and softer is not the fix. The off-track limit is max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4), so body_width cannot widen it. My diagnosis: the sensor array spans only ±0.04 m. Beyond about 0.03 m of offset the outer sensors stop seeing tape, so the sum of readings drops and the controller loses the line at speed. Iteration 6 proposed a wider array but was never raced, so this is still untested.

Changes from iteration 2: (1) Sensor x spread widens to -0.06, -0.03, 0, 0.03, 0.06 at y 0.04 with size 0.012, so tape stays visible at larger offsets. Sensor height and footprint stay as in the best design. (2) Because the same weights now respond to a wider spread, the per-metre steering gain falls. I keep kp at 3.0 to hold the effective gain near iteration 2's level. (3) kd rises from 0.5 to 0.8 to damp the overshoot that caused the max_error spikes. (4) base_speed stays at 1.4, since speed was not the limiting factor. ki stays 0 and line_loss stays last_direction. Geometry otherwise matches iteration 2.

Expected result: fewer line-loss excursions, so progress on the s-bend and slalom should rise well above 0.04 and the oval should exceed 0.22. A first finish is possible but not expected. Main risk: the wider spread may soften correction on tight bends, which max_error and progress in the next race should show.
